title: Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) : Progress towards poliomyelitis eradication, WHO Western Pacific Region, January 1996-September 1997 = Programme élargi de vaccination (PEV) : Progrès réalisés vers l’éradication de la poliomyélite, Région OMS du Pacifique occidental, janvier 1996-septembre 1997

sections.title: Page 1

summary.text: Begins a bilingual English–French Weekly Epidemiological Record report on progress towards polio eradication in the WHO Western Pacific Region, January 1996 to September 1997, noting cases fell from 5,963 in 1990 to 197 in 1996. It describes routine oral polio vaccine coverage rising to 95% and the start of supplementary immunization activities.

sections.extract: Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) Progress towards poliomyelitis eradication, WHO Western Pacific Region, January 1996-September 1997 In 1988, the World Health Assembly adopted the goal of global poliomyelitis eradication by the year 2000. This goal was subsequently endorsed in each of the 6 WHO Regions, including the Western Pacific Region (WPR). Since 1988, substantial progress has been achieved towards

sections.title: Page 2

summary.text: Describes national and sub-national immunization days across the polio-endemic countries of the Western Pacific Region and high-risk response immunizations to eliminate the last reservoirs, focused on the Mekong delta and Tonle Sap area of Cambodia and Viet Nam. It also begins reporting acute flaccid paralysis (AFP) surveillance results for 1997. The report text is given in parallel English and French.

All other poliomyelitis-endemic countries in the Region, with the exception of Papua New Guinea, have conducted at least 3 years of NIDs, including Cambodia (1994-1997), Mongolia (1994-1996), the Lao People’s Democratic Republic (1994-1997), the Philippines (1993- 1997) and Viet Nam (1993-1997).

sections.title: Page 3

summary.text: Reports that 9 of 3,796 acute flaccid paralysis cases in 1997 were confirmed as wild poliovirus, mostly in Cambodia with one in Viet Nam, and that no wild virus had been found since March 1997. It is followed in French and includes a map caption for high-risk immunization areas.

sections.title: Page 5

summary.text: Reports that most recently endemic countries met the minimum AFP surveillance rate and stool-specimen targets, Papua New Guinea being the exception. It describes the regional polio laboratory network, its proficiency testing and faster turnaround of virus typing results. It then turns to certification of polio eradication, with the English text repeated in French.

sections.extract: All recently endemic countries (except for Papua New Guinea) have reached or exceeded the WHO-established minimum rate of AFP indicating a sensitive surveillance system (at least 1 non-poliomyelitis AFP case per 100 000 children aged under 15 years [Table 1]). sections.title: Page 6

summary.text: Discusses lessons from the Western Pacific polio programme, including the use of surveillance mapping to target high-risk immunization areas, detailed district-level planning, and active AFP case searching in health facilities. It explains how these measures improved sensitivity and timeliness. The French version follows, ending with steps countries are taking to prevent any new indigenous wild-virus case from 1998.

sections.extract: Enhanced surveillance has been critical to target in- tense immunization activities to the last areas with known or suspected circulation of wild poliovirus. Detailed and timely information on AFP cases is now available to pro- gramme managers, and rapid action has been taken wherever wild virus transmission is suspected. summary.text: Concludes the bilingual polio report, noting regional confidence in near-certification standards but concern about sustaining surveillance, funding and national priority until global certification. It credits the source as a WHO Western Pacific Regional Office report also published in MMWR.

narratives.en: Bilingual (English/French) map of Cambodia, southern Lao People's Democratic Republic and southern Viet Nam showing districts included in high-risk-area immunization activities (HRRIs), May–July 1997 (shaded), and locations of wild poliovirus in 1997 (stars), most around Phnom Penh and in Cambodia. Labels give children immunized: 75 000 in Lao PDR, 1.1 million in Cambodia and 1 million in Viet Nam.
narratives.ar: خريطة ثنائية اللغة (الإنكليزية/الفرنسية) لكمبوديا وجنوب جمهورية لاو الديمقراطية الشعبية وجنوب فييت نام، تبين المقاطعات المشمولة بأنشطة التمنيع في المناطق العالية الخطورة، أيار/مايو–تموز/يوليو 1997 (مظللة)، ومواقع فيروس شلل الأطفال البري في عام 1997 (نجوم)، ومعظمها حول بنوم بنه وفي كمبوديا. وتبين التسميات عدد الأطفال الذين جرى تمنيعهم: 75000 في جمهورية لاو، و1.1 مليون في كمبوديا، ومليون في فييت نام.
narratives.zh: 英法双语地图，显示柬埔寨、老挝人民民主共和国南部和越南南部1997年5–7月纳入高风险地区免疫活动（HRRIs）的地区（阴影）以及1997年野生脊灰病毒的发现地点（星号），多数位于金边周围和柬埔寨境内。标注显示免疫儿童人数：老挝7.5万、柬埔寨110万、越南100万。
narratives.es: Mapa bilingüe (inglés/francés) de Camboya, el sur de la República Democrática Popular Lao y el sur de Viet Nam que muestra los distritos incluidos en las actividades de inmunización en zonas de alto riesgo (HRRI), mayo-julio de 1997 (sombreados), y la ubicación del poliovirus salvaje en 1997 (estrellas), la mayoría alrededor de Phnom Penh y en Camboya. Las etiquetas indican los niños vacunados: 75 000 en la RDP Lao, 1,1 millones en Camboya y 1 millón en Viet Nam.
narratives.fr: Carte bilingue (anglais/français) du Cambodge, du sud de la République démocratique populaire lao et du sud du Viet Nam montrant les districts inclus dans les activités de vaccination en zones à haut risque (VSHR), mai-juillet 1997 (en grisé), et les localisations de poliovirus sauvage en 1997 (étoiles), pour la plupart autour de Phnom Penh et au Cambodge. Les étiquettes indiquent les enfants vaccinés : 75 000 en RDP lao, 1,1 million au Cambodge et 1 million au Viet Nam.
narratives.ru: Двуязычная (англо-французская) карта Камбоджи, южной части Лаосской Народно-Демократической Республики и южного Вьетнама, показывающая районы, охваченные иммунизацией в зонах высокого риска (HRRI) в мае–июле 1997 г. (заштрихованы), и места выявления дикого полиовируса в 1997 г. (звёзды), большей частью вокруг Пномпеня и в Камбодже. Подписи указывают число иммунизированных детей: 75 000 в Лаосе, 1,1 млн в Камбодже и 1 млн во Вьетнаме.
